title: CLO International Academic Month Issue 2 (Part 1) Digital Technology and Sustainable Fashion Development
description: The second episode of Academic Month videos is now online! A conversation with the dean of Wuhan Textile University discussing the sustainable development that digital technology brings to the fashion industry.
transcript:
Hello, teachers and students, good evening. I am Tao Hui from the College of Fashion at Wuhan Fanzhi University.  
Thank you very much to CLO Shanghai for providing such an excellent academic exchange and a platform for talent training today.  

What I want to share with you today is how digital technology and fashion can continue to develop together.  
As the host just mentioned, digital technology has become an important driving force in today’s era.  
In the process of sustainable development, digital technology and sustainability are inseparable.  
So when we discuss digital technology and sustainable development today,  
I would first like to talk with you about what sustainable fashion and development mean.  

Let me show you a process chart.  
Let us understand the concept of sustainable fashion.  
What is sustainable fashion and development?  

In 1962, American artist Rachel Carson published her influential book, *Silent Spring*, which was about the initial call for human environmental protection.  
In modern language, it is called the voice of the youth.  
Then in 1971, after her focus on real-world design was published by Victor Papanek,  
some sustainable design movements also began to emerge.  
In 1991, international brands Patagonia and Esprit  
held their first fashion exhibitions.  
This was the very first annual event of its kind.  
Fashion 2020 marks a turning point.  
The fashion industry began to pay attention to sustainability.  

In 2009, the so-called Copenhagen Sustainable Fashion Highline Forum  
initiated the D’Avers Forum in the fashion industry,  
which truly opened the door for sustainable development within fashion.  

In 2019, the United States and Europe established the Sustainable Fashion Alliance  
to address the environmental crisis caused by fast fashion.  

From this brief introduction, it has been half a century since 1962.  
Modern people have been working hard to protect the environment.  
Let’s take a look.  

With the promotion of sustainable fashion,  
many effective measures have been realized.  
Let me give you an example.  

Currently, the global fashion industry’s status—  
you may also be familiar with it—  
due to the influence of trans-fashion,  
fashion consumption has increased.  
Institutions predict that by 2050,  
total clothing sales will reach 1.6 billion items,  
which is more than three times the current amount.  

At the same time, the production methods in the textile industry  
have caused waste and environmental pollution,  
which is a more serious problem.  

Regarding the current state of the fashion industry,  
some very effective measures have been implemented.  

First, we see that in 2018,  
New York Fashion Week was established with a critical emphasis:  
all products and works must be organic or renewable.  
Based on this threshold and these elements,  
all products participating in Fashion Week must be sustainable.  

At the same time, there are now endless forums and institutions focusing on sustainability.  

We have made sustainable fashion a priority.  
It is worth mentioning that in 2021,  
during the Fourth World Exports Forum,  
the International Exports Forum of China  
established the International Exports Forum of China for Sustainable Fashion and Lifestyle Professional Cooperation.  

So sometimes we can see that the Chinese fashion industry  
has already placed sustainable fashion lifestyle  
at the highest level of current life.  

What we observe are many effective measures and policies for the sustainable development of fashion,  
as well as related activities.  

At the same time, we can also look at and understand  
the current trends in sustainable fashion after many years of development.  

Let’s take a look now.  

There are mainly six representative trends.  

The first is the movement from cross-border to borderless.  
For example,  
we all know the fashion of fashion,  
or sports fashion,  
or high-end fashion,  
are in a fluid, floating state.  
At the same time, the fusion of fashion and high-end  
has moved from two borders to borderless,  
and from the original two borders to four borders,  
and now to borderless.  
This kind of promotion,  
the integration of marketing and social aspects,  
has become the first point we want to mention: from cross-border to borderless.  

The second point is that design plays an increasingly important role.  
In the past, designers focused on  
making products sellable  
and providing more aesthetic appeal.  
Now, the role of designers has changed.  
In sustainable fashion development, designers should become pioneers.  
The second role is to be transmitters, educators, and promoters.  
For example, we see that Nike and Burberry’s current CEOs actually have design backgrounds.  
So the future of the world is more about the business of design.  

The third point is that high technology is penetrating the clothing industry.  
Everyone knows about early digital printing, laser cutting,  
and even 3D printing in the fashion world.  
Of course, 3D printing is expected to develop in the future,  
but it cannot completely replace design.  
So, as we said, design remains very important.  

The fourth trend is that sustainable fast fashion will become mainstream.  
We also know that many fast fashion brands  
are characterized by low prices and high sales.  
Their rapid response leads consumers to buy quickly and discard quickly,  
which causes a rapid increase in waste.  
Now, sustainable fast fashion is emphasized.  
In the past, more attention was focused on commercial interests, cost-efficiency, and low costs.  
A low-cost product must, from a certain perspective, be sustainable.  
We are responsible for it.  
So now, it is called sustainable fast fashion.  

Sustainability involves environmental protection, worker rights, public welfare, logistics, and production line issues.  
We have established a fast supply chain platform providing design, transparency, board design, and production.  
For example, legendary manufacturing, designers, factories, and material suppliers all collaborate on this medium-sized platform involving assembly and manufacturing.  

We also see more fast fashion brands developing in a high-end direction,  
paying more attention to quality and meeting the highest consumer demands.  

At the same time, the sustainability aspect is changing.  
In the past, we have seen competition among entrepreneurs.  
Now, over time, we prove that cooperative relationships exist.  
This is a pure relationship.  

Online search and online experience,  
through virtual digital technology,  
virtual mature experiences,  
and then offline physical experiences follow.  

The sixth point is transparency in the industry chain.  
There is a tracking code that allows us to understand the production process of a product and its micro-products.  
Is it sustainable?  

What I have simply introduced is the trend in sustainable fashion development.  

Then we focus on sustainable development within the fashion industry chain.  

I summarize it in five aspects:  
First, material development.  
Second, production processes.  
Third, sales and marketing.  
Fourth, recycling—  
this is the stage when the product’s life is ending.  
How to reuse it?  
Lastly, design responsibility.  

Designers in sustainable fashion must take responsibility.  
Later, I will share more on this topic.  

We see four examples here.  
In each section, we are practicing sustainable fashion.  
We can integrate and act throughout this process.  
Many people may think sustainability is only about environmental meetings: recycling and reuse.  
But in fact, sustainability is integrated into every part of the fashion industry.  

Let’s look at an example.  
In the 2016 Spring and Summer press conference of Hanwayang,  
they showed a water-soluble fashion line emphasizing solubility.  
This is a designer’s exploration of how to use materials that degrade faster.  

Many designers are constantly exploring and understanding how to develop more raw materials with biological regenerative properties for fashion design and industry.  

In marketing, we see London sustainable entrepreneur Tara Poppins,  
who created the Body Ones shopping network,  
which emphasizes accurate purchasing.  
Effective purchasing should avoid repetition and inefficiency.  
This is one of her intentions.  

An American brand, Avalance, emphasizes transparent marketing.  
For example, take a belt:  
from raw material, buckle, sewing, to shipping—  
all costs are clearly marked on the product,  
so consumers understand where their money goes and costs are minimized.  
There is no need to make purchases with excessive design complexity.  
Simplification is a key feature.  

If interested, you can look into this further.  

In the post-sale section,  
for example, H&M, together with our National Fashion University Fashion Academy,  
has a recovery plan for jeans.  
We conducted a survey:  
everyone, at least at a certain age, owns seven or eight pairs of jeans.  
Jeans have a relatively long lifespan but are changing in use.  

Together with National Fashion University, we have joint activities upgrading jeans into art.  
At the 2014 World Fashion Conference held at our school,  
this art was gifted to guests.  

From this simple introduction,  
we understand the life cycle of a garment:  
from raw material acquisition, through consumption, to end of use.  
There is still much work to be done.  

We have already discussed several aspects,  
but these may already be familiar to everyone.  

In this industry, for all of you,  
the sustainable development path is familiar.  
We also feel that digital technology is clearly becoming a new growth point for sustainable development.  

Now, let’s look at how digital technology assists sustainable fashion development.  

Here is a case many are familiar with:  
the new design by Dutch designer Iris van Herpen.  
At her 2019 press conference, she showcased 3D printing technology.  

Early 3D printing technology was revolutionary and subversive, mainly used in industrial products in solidified form.  
With continuous improvements in printing technology and diversified materials,  
its application in clothing has increased significantly.  

This technology effectively satisfies customer needs for personalized design.  
If we buy clothes more accurately,  
we will grow deeper attachment to them,  
and they will not be easily discarded.  

Let’s look at how 3D printing technology can impact our future and sustainability.  
I believe our online audience will feel excited seeing such works,  
and hope to create suitable 3D printed pieces themselves.  

When talking about 3D printing, material is very important.  
In the future, if materials can be more organic, reduced, biological, or reusable,  
such micro-materials will definitely become an effective engine for fashion development.  

Let’s look at the 3D printing company Simplify.  
It studies natural materials and prints 3D shoes.  
These shoes satisfy traditional needs and comfort requirements.  
Material breakthroughs for future 3D printed fashion products are not far away, especially with popularization.  

In distribution, more influential is the app—  
a digital printer developed by the post office—  
allowing customers unwilling to go out or to stores to shop online and experience products virtually.  

As virtual printing matures, the sense of experience strengthens,  
making consumer shopping more accurate.  

Research shows online shopping for clothing remains popular because  
people like the images, but trying clothes on usually feels less satisfying.  

Technologies such as 3D scanning, personalization, and brand high-end personalization improve this.  
From personal experience, I visited a store with a 3D scanning space:  
in two minutes, they scanned my body and provided accurate data,  
along with a review and purchase suggestions.  

Based on this data, you can select styles online or in physical stores, try on clothes, and then purchase.  
Custom-fit garments are then produced.  

This process makes shopping more precise and consumers more satisfied.  

Clothing sharing is also a hot topic recently.  
In China, brands like One or Three, a new brand founded in 2009,  
received invitations to fashion summits and dialogues.  

We all know especially women have clothes they cherish but hesitate to discard.  
If used for exchange, these clothes can regain value and offer new clothing experiences.  
Clothing sharing is an important recommendation for sustainable development.  

We conducted a survey: many women share jackets and other clothes,  
mainly outerwear.  

In the U.S., clothing exchange is also common.  
For example, “I no longer need this dress; it’s a pity to throw it away.”  

Especially now, families with children find it important that baby clothes are safe and comfortable.  
After children outgrow them, exchanging or giving away clothes through online platforms is useful.  

This is a very important aspect of sustainable fashion.  

At the beginning, we talked about how the mode of use, manufacturing, and dispensing has evolved into a circular model.  
We can see this in the picture.  
Designing for this function is the most important.  

As I mentioned earlier, design is the soul of sustainable fashion development.  

So let’s look again:  
What principles should sustainable design follow?  

First is reuse—products should be long-lasting and repeatedly functional.  
This is a key consideration in design.  

Second is recycling—reusing materials.  
For example, after garments are no longer needed, raw materials can be reused rather than discarded.  

Third is recovery—recycling and designing for end-of-life,  
effectively returning materials to nature.  

Fourth is re-creation—redesign.  
This emphasizes that if original designs can be stored and reused digitally,  
digital design becomes central.  

For example, Professor Jiang Minghua of Wuhan University and the University of Hong Kong designed a digitalized, re-creatable design.  
This digital form is fixed yet can be recreated precisely and simply.  

If we have such digitalized clothes, no one would easily discard them.  

Let’s watch another video made by our students.  
We train students to be savvy with social media.  
They created this video mainly for public viewing.  

Look at the clothes—they are very fashionable.  
For example, for work, I wear a formal dress.  

Let’s consider the case of 361, a well-known Chinese sports brand.  
Since 2015, it has used 3D clothing software for design.  
This design method shows the product effect clearly and is very popular.  

From design to garment production, this is an effective way to reduce waste and shorten processes.  
It also creates a digitized database of designers’ work.  
When needed, data can be transferred at any time for new designs.  

This is a very important point for future fashion development.  

Let me introduce our university again.  
We are from Wuhan University.  
We have focused on digital technology and sustainable design education for years.  
Sustainable development in fashion is a core characteristic of our education.  

In our department, we have joint education projects with foreign schools on sustainable fashion development,  
including the University of Manchester in the UK.  
We have been undertaking sustainable design projects since 2019.  

At the same time, we promote international meetings.  
Graduate students have started courses on sustainability.  
We also held a world environmental design competition  
and an international meeting with Manchester City University  
focused on fashion and climate change.  

As mentioned, our department started a virtual online course  
to help students master sustainability comprehensively.  

Here is some course homework.  
You can see some products introduced in class.  
For our students, this is a starting point to master skills,  
and a talent guarantee for future industry development.  

This is a special design by senior students using 3D cloth technology.  
Graduate students also use 3D cloth to create traditional-style clothing designs.  
We use 3D cloth technology in study and life.  

This is a very good 3D cloth presentation.  
Graduate students created sustainable clothing designs using 3D cloth.  
Senior students made similar presentations.  

Regarding the nature of sustainable fashion, from my personal view,  
it should focus on two aspects:  
one is the micro-level extension of product life cycle;  
the second is material condition—  
how it can be reduced at end-of-life and returned to nature.  

From a broader perspective,  
the first goal is to satisfy people’s pursuit of the best life.  
The second is to develop from excellent traditional national culture.  

Based on this, we conducted an experiment:  
an anti-stress virtual imitation experiment course,  
where students learn culture through traditional clothing experience.  
They also master virtual imitation technology,  
using 3D for digital clothing design.  

This is in cooperation with the Hubei City Hall Party Committee.  
We made virtual imitations of Han Junmin and Master Chen Bohua’s red-striped flower champagne queen dresses.  
The imitation is very accurate.  
This is for those planning trips or events.  

Some products are hard to preserve physically.  
After building a database, we can produce more copies.  
This helps preserve tradition.  
You can also learn more online.  

Here is one example of such imitation.  
We include not only images but embroidery, all very well recreated.  

We also do traditional clothing digital virtual imitation.  
For example, this is a big red non-fish patterned women’s long shirt, and this is a modern version.  
Recently, we dug up a cotton dress and a traditional clothing database.  

The introduction I gave, about sustainable fashion development  
and how digital technology helps the fashion industry,  
shows that design plays a key role.  

With digital technology’s participation and assistance,  
design will continue to play a significant role in the entire fashion industry chain,  
and will become more prominent in the future.  

There is a sentence I want to share:  
our fashion’s sustainable development is actually about satisfying people’s desire for the best life.  
Satisfying people’s best life is our goal.  

With the arrival of the digital age,  
digital technology has become an important driver and engine in fashion development.  

Therefore, digital design education and sustainable fashion industry development  
are long-standing demands for talent.  

Look at this video.  
This is a work by a Japanese designer published in 2021.  
Through this video,  
we see the value of digital software in 3D design,  
including fabric exchange, expression of feeling, and material effects—all very clear.  

This is similar to the 361 product design I mentioned earlier,  
where a series of products are directly introduced.  

Dear audience, friends, teachers, and students,  
that is all for my sharing today.  
Thank you all.  

Thank you for watching.  
See you in the next video.  
Bye-bye.

chunks.title: CLO International Academic Month Issue 2 (Part 1) Digital Technology and Sustainable Fashion Development
chunks.content: ## Introduction to Digital Technology and Sustainable Fashion Development This section introduces the integration of digital technology with sustainable fashion development, highlighting the inseparable relationship between sustainability and technological advancement in the fashion industry. Digital technology has become a pivotal force driving sustainable development in fashion. Sustainable fashion refers to practices that minimize environmental impact while promoting social responsibility throughout the fashion lifecycle. The concept has evolved over decades, beginning with environmental awareness sparked by Rachel Carson's 1962 book *Silent Spring*, which called for human environmental protection. The sustainable design movement gained momentum with Victor Papanek’s work in 1971 and significant industry events, such as Patagonia and Esprit’s first sustainable fashion exhibitions in 1991. By 2020, sustainability became a central focus within the fashion industry. Key milestones include the 2009 Copenhagen Sustainable Fashion Highline Forum that opened doors for sustainable fashion development, and the 2019 establishment of the Sustainable Fashion Alliance in the US and Europe, addressing environmental crises caused by fast fashion. These efforts reflect over half a century of growing environmental consciousness in fashion. ## Global Fashion Industry Challenges and Sustainable Measures This section discusses the current challenges posed by fast fashion and the measures taken by the industry to promote sustainability, focusing on production, consumption, and policy responses. The global fashion industry faces significant challenges due to increased consumption driven by fast fashion. Predictions estimate that by 2050, total clothing sales will reach 1.6 billion items—more than three times current levels. This surge exacerbates waste and environmental pollution from traditional textile production methods. Effective measures have been implemented to address these issues. For example, since 2018, New York Fashion Week requires all participating products to be organic or renewable, enforcing strict sustainability criteria. Numerous forums and institutions now prioritize sustainable fashion, exemplified by the 2021 International Exports Forum of China for Sustainable Fashion and Lifestyle Professional Cooperation, underscoring China’s commitment to sustainable lifestyles. These efforts demonstrate how sustainability has become a priority in policies, industry standards, and collaborative activities worldwide. ## Trends in Sustainable Fashion Development This section outlines six key trends shaping sustainable fashion, including cross-border integration, designer roles, technology adoption, sustainable fast fashion, collaboration, and supply chain transparency. 1. **From Cross-Border to Borderless Fashion** Fashion categories such as sports, high-end, and casual wear have evolved from segmented markets to fluid, borderless integration. This fusion enhances marketing strategies and social engagement. 2. **Evolving Role of Designers** Designers now act as pioneers, educators, and promoters of sustainable fashion, moving beyond aesthetics and sales. Notably, CEOs with design backgrounds at Nike and Burberry illustrate the growing business significance of design. 3. **Technology Penetration in Clothing** Technologies like digital printing, laser cutting, and 3D printing are increasingly utilized in fashion. While 3D printing is promising, it complements rather than replaces traditional design. 4. **Rise of Sustainable Fast Fashion** Fast fashion brands, known for low cost and rapid turnover, are shifting towards sustainability, balancing commercial interests with environmental responsibility.

chunks.title: CLO International Academic Month Issue 2 (Part 1) Digital Technology and Sustainable Fashion Development
chunks.content: **Evolving Role of Designers** Designers now act as pioneers, educators, and promoters of sustainable fashion, moving beyond aesthetics and sales. Notably, CEOs with design backgrounds at Nike and Burberry illustrate the growing business significance of design. 3. **Technology Penetration in Clothing** Technologies like digital printing, laser cutting, and 3D printing are increasingly utilized in fashion. While 3D printing is promising, it complements rather than replaces traditional design. 4. **Rise of Sustainable Fast Fashion** Fast fashion brands, known for low cost and rapid turnover, are shifting towards sustainability, balancing commercial interests with environmental responsibility. Sustainable fast fashion integrates worker rights, public welfare, logistics, and transparent production processes. 5. **Collaborative Industry Relationships** Competitive entrepreneurial dynamics are giving way to cooperative partnerships, fostering shared platforms for design, manufacturing, and materials supply. 6. **Supply Chain Transparency** The use of tracking codes enables consumers and stakeholders to trace product origins and verify sustainability claims across the supply chain. ## Sustainable Development in the Fashion Industry Chain This section breaks down sustainable fashion into five core components: material development, production processes, sales and marketing, recycling, and design responsibility. - **Material Development:** Focus on creating organic, renewable, and biodegradable materials. - **Production Processes:** Adoption of eco-friendly manufacturing techniques. - **Sales and Marketing:** Emphasis on transparent and efficient consumer engagement to reduce waste. - **Recycling:** Strategies for product end-of-life reuse and repurposing. - **Design Responsibility:** Designers are accountable for ensuring sustainability throughout the product lifecycle. Examples illustrating these stages include: - **Material Innovation:** Hanwayang’s 2016 Spring/Summer water-soluble fashion line explores degradable materials. - **Marketing Transparency:** London entrepreneur Tara Poppins' Body Ones network promotes efficient purchasing, while US brand Avalance transparently details product costs from raw materials to shipping. - **Post-Sale Recycling:** H&M collaborates with National Fashion University to recover and repurpose jeans, transforming them into art, extending product life and cultural value. These examples demonstrate sustainability’s integration into all fashion industry segments, beyond mere recycling. ## Digital Technology's Role in Sustainable Fashion This section explains how digital technology, especially 3D printing and virtual experiences, supports sustainable fashion by enhancing design precision, personalization, and consumer engagement. Dutch designer Iris van Herpen showcased 3D printing technology in 2019, demonstrating its revolutionary potential in fashion. Advances in 3D printing materials and techniques allow for personalized clothing production, fostering consumer attachment and reducing waste. Companies like Simplify utilize natural materials to produce comfortable 3D-printed shoes, signaling material innovation’s role in future sustainable fashion. Digital printing apps developed by postal services enable virtual product experiences and online shopping, improving customer convenience and accuracy. Technologies such as 3D scanning enable precise body measurements, allowing consumers to select and try on clothes virtually before purchase, increasing satisfaction and reducing returns. This personalization is key to sustainable consumption. Additionally, clothing sharing platforms are growing, with brands like One or Three in China promoting reuse and exchange of cherished garments, particularly outerwear and children’s clothing, supporting circular fashion models.

chunks.content: Digital printing apps developed by postal services enable virtual product experiences and online shopping, improving customer convenience and accuracy. Technologies such as 3D scanning enable precise body measurements, allowing consumers to select and try on clothes virtually before purchase, increasing satisfaction and reducing returns. This personalization is key to sustainable consumption. Additionally, clothing sharing platforms are growing, with brands like One or Three in China promoting reuse and exchange of cherished garments, particularly outerwear and children’s clothing, supporting circular fashion models. ## Principles of Sustainable Fashion Design This section outlines fundamental principles guiding sustainable fashion design, emphasizing reuse, recycling, recovery, and digital re-creation. 1. **Reuse:** Designing products for durability and repeated use. 2. **Recycling:** Incorporating reclaimed materials into new garments. 3. **Recovery:** Planning for end-of-life material return to natural cycles. 4. **Re-creation:** Utilizing digital design to store and recreate garments, reducing physical waste. A notable example is the digitalized, re-creatable designs by Professor Jiang Minghua (Wuhan University and University of Hong Kong), which enable precise digital garment reproduction, discouraging disposal. Digital design technologies such as 3D cloth simulation are used extensively in education and practice at Wuhan University, where students create sustainable clothing collections digitally, reinforcing design’s central role in sustainable fashion. ## Education and Research in Digital and Sustainable Fashion This section highlights Wuhan University’s initiatives in sustainable fashion education, international collaboration, and digital design research. Wuhan University’s College of Fashion has prioritized digital technology and sustainable design for years, collaborating with international institutions like the University of Manchester. Since 2019, they have engaged in sustainable design projects and environmental design competitions focused on fashion and climate change. Graduate courses emphasize sustainability, supported by virtual online classes to comprehensively train students. Student projects include 3D cloth technology applications in traditional and modern clothing design, fostering skills essential for future industry demands. Experiments like the anti-stress virtual imitation course combine traditional cultural education with 3D digital clothing design, preserving heritage through accurate virtual reproductions of garments, including embroidery and fabric details. Cooperation with the Hubei City Hall Party Committee facilitates these efforts, enabling digital preservation and reproduction of culturally significant attire. ## Summary: Digital Technology as a Driver for Sustainable Fashion Design remains the soul of sustainable fashion development, with digital technology enhancing design capabilities, supply chain transparency, and consumer engagement. The dual goals are extending product lifecycles and reducing environmental impact through material innovation and circular economy practices. Sustainable fashion aims to satisfy people’s pursuit of the best quality of life while drawing from traditional cultural excellence. Digital tools, including 3D printing, scanning, and virtual experiences, empower designers and consumers alike, making sustainability a practical and integral part of fashion’s future. Education and talent cultivation in digital design and sustainability are critical for advancing the industry. Examples from Chinese sports brand 361 demonstrate how 3D clothing software shortens production cycles and reduces waste, creating valuable digitized design assets.

Companies like Simplify utilize natural materials to produce comfortable 3D-printed shoes, signaling material innovation’s role in future sustainable fashion. Digital printing apps developed by postal services enable virtual product experiences and online shopping, improving customer convenience and accuracy. Technologies such as 3D scanning enable precise body measurements, allowing consumers to select and try on clothes virtually before purchase, increasing satisfaction and reducing returns. This personalization is key to sustainable consumption. Additionally, clothing sharing platforms are growing, with brands like One or Three in China promoting reuse and exchange of cherished garments, particularly outerwear and children’s clothing, supporting circular fashion models. ## Principles of Sustainable Fashion Design This section outlines fundamental principles guiding sustainable fashion design, emphasizing reuse, recycling, recovery, and digital re-creation. 1. **Reuse:** Designing products for durability and repeated use. 2. **Recycling:** Incorporating reclaimed materials into new garments. 3. **Recovery:** Planning for end-of-life material return to natural cycles. 4. **Re-creation:** Utilizing digital design to store and recreate garments, reducing physical waste. A notable example is the digitalized, re-creatable designs by Professor Jiang Minghua (Wuhan University and University of Hong Kong), which enable precise digital garment reproduction, discouraging disposal. Digital design technologies such as 3D cloth simulation are used extensively in education and practice at Wuhan University, where students create sustainable clothing collections digitally, reinforcing design’s central role in sustainable fashion. ## Education and Research in Digital and Sustainable Fashion This section highlights Wuhan University’s initiatives in sustainable fashion education, international collaboration, and digital design research. Wuhan University’s College of Fashion has prioritized digital technology and sustainable design for years, collaborating with international institutions like the University of Manchester. Since 2019, they have engaged in sustainable design projects and environmental design competitions focused on fashion and climate change. Graduate courses emphasize sustainability, supported by virtual online classes to comprehensively train students. Student projects include 3D cloth technology applications in traditional and modern clothing design, fostering skills essential for future industry demands. Experiments like the anti-stress virtual imitation course combine traditional cultural education with 3D digital clothing design, preserving heritage through accurate virtual reproductions of garments, including embroidery and fabric details. Cooperation with the Hubei City Hall Party Committee facilitates these efforts, enabling digital preservation and reproduction of culturally significant attire. ## Summary: Digital Technology as a Driver for Sustainable Fashion Design remains the soul of sustainable fashion development, with digital technology enhancing design capabilities, supply chain transparency, and consumer engagement. The dual goals are extending product lifecycles and reducing environmental impact through material innovation and circular economy practices. Sustainable fashion aims to satisfy people’s pursuit of the best quality of life while drawing from traditional cultural excellence. Digital tools, including 3D printing, scanning, and virtual experiences, empower designers and consumers alike, making sustainability a practical and integral part of fashion’s future. Education and talent cultivation in digital design and sustainability are critical for advancing the industry. Examples from Chinese sports brand 361 demonstrate how 3D clothing software shortens production cycles and reduces waste, creating valuable digitized design assets. Ultimately, the convergence of digital technology and sustainable fashion represents a long-term strategy for innovation, environmental stewardship, and cultural preservation in the global fashion industry.
